newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour forecasts 150,000 new year job losses.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour forecasts 150,000 new year job losses.

text.p: More than 150,000 British workers will lose their jobs in the coming months, the opposition Labour Party said on Monday.

The job losses will cover all areas of the economy including construction, financial services, retail and manufacturing industries and public services, a Labour statement said. They will total 151,674.
Labour's figures totted up a breakdown of redundancies planned by major British companies and the public sector, compiled from employers' press releases and announcements.

"These figures show why job insecurity plagues every office and factory in Britain and why no-one believes this government's fiddled unemployment figures," said Peter Hain, Labour employment spokesman.
He said the method of calculating unemployment figures had been changed 32 times since the Conservative government first came to power in 1979.

Official figures show unemployment in Britain has been falling consistently for about the past four years. The unemployment rate is now 7.1 percent, well below that of continental European countries such as Germany and France.
"Redundancies continue to be announced in all areas of the economy," Hain said. The UK is losing skilled, permanent jobs and new work is part-time, temporary, and often badly paid," Hain said.
